## Champion selection (leak-free, train split only)

- **data:** training split only (800 rows); the 200-row test split is never used for selection
- **outer cv:** 5-fold stratified x 3 repeats = 15 paired folds
- **inner cv:** 5-fold, picks hyperparameters (PR-AUC) and threshold (F1) per candidate
- **selection rule:** highest mean outer-fold F1 at each candidate's own tuned threshold; must not be worse than the 'major_damage_rule' baseline; ties within 0.005 F1 broken by PR-AUC
- **significance test:** Nadeau-Bengio corrected resampled t-test (two-sided) on the paired fold differences
- **Measured champion:** `random_forest`

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Oracle external validation

Model evaluated: `random_forest`

| | Internal holdout | Oracle (external) |
|---|---|---|
| ROC-AUC | 0.792 | 0.461 |
| PR-AUC | 0.546 | 0.054 |
| Confusion matrix @ operating threshold (0.45) | — | TN 14497 / FP 0 / FN 923 / TP 0 |

Oracle ROC-AUC bootstrap 95% CI: [0.441, 0.480] (n_boot=1000) — **significantly inverted ranking** — the whole CI is below 0.5, so on Oracle the model gives genuine fraud cases systematically LOWER scores than legitimate claims. Do not describe this as 'random'.

**Statistical caveat (SH-05):** Oracle's 15,420 rows give this comparison high statistical power for what it measures — but PR-AUC's own baseline shifts with class prevalence (this project's internal fraud rate is 24.8%; Oracle's is far lower), so the internal-vs-Oracle PR-AUC gap above is not read the same way ROC-AUC's fixed 0.5 random baseline is — part of the gap reflects prevalence, not model degradation alone. The primary, prevalence-independent evidence for the generalization failure is the SHAP-weight constant-feature analysis in docs/REBUILD_NOTES.md (Oracle has no equivalent field for most of the model's top-weighted features), not the PR-AUC number alone.
